annotations.title: North Carolina (NC) appellate, practice and Business Court rules

description:
North Carolina (NC) court rules that are NOT in the General Statutes: the Rules of
Appellate Procedure, the General Rules of Practice for the Superior and District Courts,
and the Business Court Rules.

Give `citation` in any common form — "N.C. R. App. P. 30(e)", "App. R. 30", "Appellate
Rule 28(b)(6)", "Rule 2 of the General Rules of Practice", "BCR 7.2", "Business Court
Rule 7.2" — or `rule_set` + `rule`. A pinpoint returns that subdivision's text (`pinpoint`)
alongside the whole rule. `rule_set` alone lists its rules; `query` searches by topic.

The Rules of Civil Procedure and of Evidence are General Statutes (G.S. 1A-1, 8C-1): use
get_statute("1A-1, Rule 12"). The Rules of Professional Conduct are NC Administrative Code
(27 NCAC 02): use get_rule. Local rules are not covered.

Earlier versions: `as_of` reads the rule as codified then, and `compare_with` adds a
line diff between two codifications — "Appellate Rule 28 in 2019 vs today" is
citation="App. R. 28", compare_with="2019". Versions are dated by codification, not by
each amendment's effective date; the Appellate Rules go back to the January 2019
codification.

as_of.description: Read the rule as codified on this date (YYYY-MM-DD), or in this year (the first codification that year). Omit for the current text.

citation.description: A court rule in any common form, with or without a pinpoint.
examples: Rule 2 of the General Rules of Practice

compare_with.description: Diff the rule against its version on this date or in this year (same forms as `as_of`), oldest first. The diff replaces the full text in the answer and may run to twice `max_chars`.

limit.description: With `query`: maximum number of rules to return (1-25).

max_chars.description: Cut the rule's text, and its commentary, at this many characters (default 12000).

query.description: Topic search when there is no citation.

rule_set.description: "app" (Appellate Procedure), "gen" (General Rules of Practice) or "bcr" (Business Court); with `rule`, or to narrow `query`.
